officialTitle: Pembrolizumab for Early Triple-Negative Breast Cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Of the 1174 patients who underwent randomization, 784 were assigned to the pembrolizumab-chemotherapy group and 390 to the placebo-chemotherapy group.
design.notes: 2:1 randomisation. Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab/placebo with paclitaxel-carboplatin, then with AC/EC; adjuvant pembrolizumab/placebo for up to nine cycles after surgery.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding perioperative pembrolizumab to neoadjuvant chemotherapy improve pathological complete response, event-free survival and overall survival in stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer?

pico.population: Previously untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer
pico.intervention: Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab plus paclitaxel-carboplatin then anthracycline-cyclophosphamide, followed by adjuvant pembrolizumab
pico.comparator: Placebo plus the same neoadjuvant chemotherapy, followed by adjuvant placebo
pico.outcomes: Primary: pCR and EFS. Secondary: OS, safety

arms.label: Pembrolizumab-chemotherapy
arms.regimen: Pembrolizumab + paclitaxel/carboplatin → pembrolizumab + AC/EC; adjuvant pembrolizumab
arms.doseSourceQuote: We randomly assigned, in a 2:1 ratio, patients with previously untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer to receive neoadjuvant therapy with four cycles of pembrolizumab (at a dose of 200 mg) or placebo every 3 weeks plus paclitaxel and carboplatin

arms.label: Placebo-chemotherapy
arms.regimen: Placebo + paclitaxel/carboplatin → placebo + AC/EC; adjuvant placebo

publications.title: Pembrolizumab for Early Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
publications.label: pCR analysis (first interim)

publications.title: Event-free Survival with Pembrolizumab in Early Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Event-free survival (fourth interim analysis)

outcomes.sourceQuote: At the first interim analysis, among the first 602 patients who underwent randomization, the percentage of patients with a pathological complete response was 64.8% (95% confidence interval [CI], 59.9 to 69.5) in the pembrolizumab-chemotherapy group and 51.2% (95% CI, 44.1 to 58.3) in the placebo-chemotherapy group (estimated treatment difference, 13.6 percentage points; 95% CI, 5.4 to 21.8; P<0.001).

After a median follow-up of 15.5 months (range, 2.7 to 25.0), 58 of 784 patients (7.4%) in the pembrolizumab-chemotherapy group and 46 of 390 patients (11.8%) in the placebo-chemotherapy group had disease progression that precluded definitive surgery, had local or distant recurrence or a second primary tumor, or died from any cause (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.43 to 0.93).

The estimated event-free survival at 36 months was 84.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 81.7 to 86.9) in the pembrolizumab-chemotherapy group, as compared with 76.8% (95% CI, 72.2 to 80.7) in the placebo-chemotherapy group (hazard ratio for event or death, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.48 to 0.82; P<0.001).

The estimated overall survival at 60 months was 86.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 84.0 to 88.8) in the pembrolizumab-chemotherapy group, as compared with 81.7% (95% CI, 77.5 to 85.2) in the placebo-chemotherapy group (P = 0.002).

safety.description: Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or higher (all phases)
safety.sourceQuote: Across all treatment phases, the incidence of treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or higher was 78.0% in the pembrolizumab-chemotherapy group and 73.0% in the placebo-chemotherapy group, including death in 0.4% (3 patients) and 0.3% (1 patient), respectively.

Across all treatment phases, the incidence of treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or higher was 78.0% in the pembrolizumab-chemotherapy group and 73.0% in the placebo-chemotherapy group, including death in 0.4% (3 patients) and 0.3% (1 patient), respectively.

strengths: Consistent benefit across pCR, EFS and OS
limitations: Design cannot separate the contribution of the neoadjuvant versus the adjuvant pembrolizumab phase
Immune-related toxicity in a curative-intent population
Intensive multi-agent chemotherapy backbone including carboplatin

clinicalImplications.text: Established perioperative pembrolizumab with platinum-containing neoadjuvant chemotherapy as a standard for stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer, with an overall survival benefit at final analysis.

tumourBoardPearl.text: KEYNOTE-522 tested a perioperative package — neoadjuvant pembrolizumab with platinum-containing chemotherapy followed by adjuvant pembrolizumab; the design does not isolate the contribution of the adjuvant phase.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from PubMed abstracts of PMIDs 32101663, 35139274 and 39282906. PD-L1 subgroup data are not reported in these abstracts and were not ingested.
